parts.context: Owen, a systems analyst, asks Clara, the manager of a gym, about the booking app she wants.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: Thanks for meeting me, Clara. I'd like to ask some questions about the booking app you want for the gym.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: First, what should members be able to do with the app?

script.speaker: Clara
script.text: Mainly book classes. At the moment, people have to phone reception, and the phone is always busy. We want members to book a place in a class in just a few seconds.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: Do members need to log in?

script.speaker: Clara
script.text: Yes, they have to log in with their membership number and a password. We don't want visitors to book classes.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: OK. What happens if a class is full?

script.speaker: Clara
script.text: The app should put the member on a waiting list. And if someone cancels, the next person on the list should get a message.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: That's clear. Do you need any payment features?

script.speaker: Clara
script.text: No. Members pay every month at reception, so the app doesn't need to take payments. But I'd like it to show the class timetable for the whole week.

script.speaker: Clara
script.text: Yes. Our instructors want the app to tell them how many people are coming to each class.

script.speaker: Owen
script.text: Great. I'll write the specification and send it to you on Friday.

questions.stem: Why does Clara want a booking app?

options.text: The reception phone is always busy.

questions.explanation: Clara nói hiện giờ hội viên phải gọi lễ tân "and the phone is always busy".

questions.stem: What do members need to log in?

options.text: An email address and a password
A membership number and a password
A name and a date of birth

questions.explanation: "they have to log in with their membership number and a password".

questions.stem: What should the app do if a class is full?

options.text: Ask the member to pay more
Put the member on a waiting list
Tell reception to phone the member

questions.explanation: "The app should put the member on a waiting list."

questions.stem: Why doesn't the app need to take payments?

options.text: Members pay every month at reception.
The bank does not allow it.

questions.explanation: "Members pay every month at reception, so the app doesn't need to take payments."

questions.stem: When will Owen send the specification?
questions.explanation: "I'll write the specification and send it to you on Friday."

parts.instructions: Listen to the presentation and answer the questions. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each answer (Questions L6–L10).
parts.context: Priya, a web designer, presents the structure of a new museum website.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Good afternoon. Today I'm going to show you the structure of the new website for the City Science Museum. Everything starts from the home page, which is linked to five main sections: Visit, Exhibitions, Learning, Shop and Contact.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: The Visit section is used most, so it is placed first in the menu. Opening times and ticket prices are shown on this page, and tickets can be bought online. In the Exhibitions section, each exhibition is given its own page with photos and a short video. Past exhibitions are kept in an archive, so they can still be seen after they close.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: The Learning section is designed for teachers. Lesson plans can be downloaded there for free. The Contact page includes a map and a form, and all messages are answered within two days.

script.speaker: Priya
script.text: Finally, every page is tested on phones and tablets, because about seventy percent of visitors use mobile devices. The site is scheduled to go live in September. Thank you.

questions.stem: How many main sections are linked to the home page?
questions.explanation: "the home page, which is linked to five main sections".
"The Visit section is used most, so it is placed first in the menu."

questions.stem: Who is the Learning section designed for?
questions.explanation: "The Learning section is designed for teachers."

questions.stem: How quickly are messages from the Contact page answered?
questions.explanation: "all messages are answered within two days".

questions.stem: When is the site scheduled to go live?
questions.explanation: "The site is scheduled to go live in September."

matching.instructions: Match the terms (1–5) with the correct definitions (A–F). There is one extra definition that you do not need (Questions 1–5).

definitions.text: To remove the mistakes from a computer program.
Website information of very high quality that you often need to pay to access.
A type of bar chart that shows when things are going to happen in a project.
The process of improving the position of a website in the results of a search engine.
A quantity in a program that can represent several different amounts.
A process of testing software in which customers use it, so that any problems will be found.

items.explanation: Gantt chart (biểu đồ Gantt) là biểu đồ thanh cho thấy khi nào các việc trong dự án diễn ra.
Beta testing (kiểm thử beta) là đưa phần mềm cho khách hàng dùng thử để tìm ra lỗi.
Debug (gỡ lỗi) là loại bỏ lỗi khỏi chương trình máy tính.
Variable (biến) là đại lượng có thể mang nhiều giá trị khác nhau.

SEO (Search Engine Optimisation, tối ưu hoá công cụ tìm kiếm) là cải thiện thứ hạng của trang web trong kết quả tìm kiếm. Định nghĩa B là của premium content (nội dung trả phí), không có trong danh sách thuật ngữ.

grammar.stem: The manager wants the developers ______ the app by Friday.
grammar.explanation: Cấu trúc want + tân ngữ + to-infinitive: "wants the developers to finish".

grammar.stem: Users ______ to log in before they can see their orders.
grammar.explanation: Chỗ trống đứng trước "to log in" nên chỉ "need (to)" đúng. "should", "must", "can" là động từ khuyết thiếu, đi thẳng với động từ nguyên mẫu, không có "to".

grammar.stem: The website ______ by thousands of people every day.
grammar.explanation: Câu bị động (có "by thousands of people"): be + quá khứ phân từ: "is visited".

grammar.stem: The new company logo ______ last week by our design team.
grammar.explanation: Bị động thì quá khứ đơn (last week, by our design team): was + quá khứ phân từ: "was designed".

grammar.stem: Clicking this button makes the video ______ again from the beginning.
grammar.explanation: make + tân ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu không "to": "makes the video start".

grammar.stem: A missing bracket in the code can cause the program ______.
grammar.explanation: cause + tân ngữ + to-infinitive: "cause the program to crash".

grammar.stem: We're due ______ the app to the client at the end of the month.
grammar.explanation: be due + to-infinitive để nói về lịch trình: "We're due to deliver".

vocabulary.stem: According to the project ______, the design stage finishes in May.
vocabulary.explanation: Schedule (lịch trình) là kế hoạch cho biết việc gì sẽ diễn ra và khi nào.

vocabulary.stem: Our teacher gave us some useful ______ on our project presentation.
vocabulary.explanation: Feedback (nhận xét, phản hồi) là lời khuyên, góp ý về mức độ thành công của một việc.

vocabulary.stem: The client has to ______ the design before the programmers start work.
vocabulary.explanation: Approve (phê duyệt) là chính thức chấp nhận một kế hoạch, bản thiết kế.

vocabulary.stem: The ______ is the first page that visitors see when they open a website.
vocabulary.explanation: Home page (trang chủ) là trang đầu tiên của trang web, thường có liên kết tới các trang khác.

vocabulary.stem: Before you contact customer support, read the ______ page, where you can find answers to common questions.
vocabulary.explanation: FAQs (Frequently Asked Questions) là trang các câu hỏi thường gặp kèm câu trả lời.

vocabulary.stem: This program has more than 50,000 ______ of code.
vocabulary.explanation: Line of code (dòng mã) là một dòng lệnh trong chương trình.

vocabulary.stem: ______ testing is done by the company that is writing the software.
vocabulary.explanation: Alpha testing (kiểm thử alpha) do chính công ty viết phần mềm thực hiện.

vocabulary.stem: The ______ describes exactly what the new software should do.
vocabulary.explanation: Specification (bản đặc tả) là mô tả chi tiết phần mềm phải làm gì.

passage.title: The Harbour Ferries App
paragraphs: Harbour Ferries runs boats between four islands. At the moment, passengers buy paper tickets at the port, and there are often long queues in summer. Last autumn, to reduce the queues, the company asked a small software firm, Bytecraft, to develop a mobile app for buying and showing tickets.

The project began in January. Bytecraft has five people working on it: a project manager, three programmers and a designer. The requirements were approved by the ferry company in February, and the programmers started writing the code in March. The most difficult part is the payment system, which has to work even when passengers have a weak phone signal at sea.

The programmers are finishing the last features this month. The app is due to be ready at the end of May, and it is scheduled to go live on 1 June, just before the busy summer season. The ferry company plans to put large posters at every port so that passengers know about the app. The posters are due to arrive in the middle of May.

There is one risk. The ferry company also wants the app to show live boat times, but this feature was added to the plan late, in April. The project manager thinks that it may not be ready by June, so the team is planning to release it in July instead. Paper tickets are going to stay available for passengers without smartphones.

questions.stem: Why did Harbour Ferries ask Bytecraft to develop an app?

options.text: To reduce the queues for tickets

questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "to reduce the queues, the company asked a small software firm, Bytecraft, to develop a mobile app". Giờ tàu trực tiếp là tính năng thêm vào sau, trong tháng Tư.
Đoạn 2: "The requirements were approved by the ferry company in February".

questions.stem: Why is the payment system the most difficult part?

options.text: Many passengers do not have smartphones.
The client changed it in April.
It must work with a weak phone signal.
It has to print paper tickets.

questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: hệ thống thanh toán "has to work even when passengers have a weak phone signal at sea".

questions.stem: When is the app scheduled to go live?
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: "it is scheduled to go live on 1 June". Cuối tháng Năm là lúc ứng dụng dự kiến làm xong.

questions.stem: What does the team plan to do with the live boat times feature?

options.text: Add it to the paper tickets

questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: "the team is planning to release it in July instead".

passageTrueFalse.instructions: Read the passage and write T (True) or F (False) (Questions 26–30).

passage.title: A Program for a Smart Greenhouse
paragraphs: A small farm near York uses a computer program to control its greenhouse. The program was written by a local student, and it reads information from three sensors every five minutes: one for temperature, one for light and one for the soil.

If the temperature goes above 28 degrees, the program makes the roof windows open. When the temperature falls below 18 degrees, it closes the windows and makes the heater switch on. Dry soil causes the water pump to start, and the pump runs for exactly two minutes each time.

At night, the program does not open the windows, even if the greenhouse is warm, because the farmer worries about animals getting inside. Every morning at seven o'clock, a short report is sent to the farmer's phone.

Last summer, a broken sensor caused the pump to run all day, and many plants were damaged. Since then, the program has had a new safety rule: the pump is never allowed to run more than ten times in one day.

questions.statement: The greenhouse program was written by a local student.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 1: "The program was written by a local student".

questions.statement: A temperature above 28 degrees makes the heater switch on.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 2: trên 28 độ thì chương trình mở cửa sổ mái; máy sưởi chỉ bật khi nhiệt độ dưới 18 độ.

questions.statement: The program opens the windows at night if the greenhouse is warm.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: "At night, the program does not open the windows, even if the greenhouse is warm".

questions.statement: The farmer receives a report every evening.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 3: báo cáo được gửi "Every morning at seven o'clock".

questions.statement: The pump is now allowed to run a maximum of ten times a day.
questions.explanation: Đoạn 4: quy tắc mới "the pump is never allowed to run more than ten times in one day".

targetGrammar: Requirements (at least two): should, have to, need to
The passive (at least one): is saved, must be reported, can be found
Schedules (at least one): be due to, be scheduled to
email.modelAnswer:
Dear Leo,

Here is what you need to check in the new delivery app. First, you have to log in with the test account. The password can be found in the project folder. Then place three test orders and check that each order is saved. You should test the app on both Android and iOS phones. Also check that the restaurant receives a message for each order. Every problem must be reported in the tracker with a screenshot. Testing is due to finish on Thursday, because the app is scheduled to go live next Monday.

Thanks,
Maya

parts.instructions: Explain how a program works. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: You wrote a simple car racing game for a programming class. Explain to your classmates what happens in the game when players do different things. Use make + object + verb (makes the car move) and cause + object + to + verb (causes the game to end).
cues: press the left or right arrow key → the car moves left or right
hit a wall → the game ends
collect a coin → the score goes up by ten points
the score reaches 100 → the next level starts
press the space bar → the game stops for a short time
requiredGrammar: make + object + bare infinitive: Pressing the arrow key makes the car move.
cause + object + to-infinitive: Hitting a wall causes the game to end.
parts.sampleAnswer: Let me explain how my game works. The player controls a small red car. Pressing the left arrow key makes the car move to the left, and the right arrow key makes it move to the right. The player has to avoid the walls, because hitting a wall causes the game to end immediately. There are gold coins on the road. Collecting a coin makes the score go up by ten points. When the score reaches one hundred, this causes the next level to start, and the car goes faster. If the player needs a break, pressing the space bar makes the game stop for a short time. Pressing it again makes the game continue. I want to add music to the game next week.

parts.instructions: Deal with the situation. Speak for 1–1.5 minutes.
parts.prompt: Your company is moving its servers to a new server room next week. Your manager asks you about the plan. Use the cues to explain what is going to happen each day. Use plan to, be due to, be scheduled to and the present continuous for future arrangements.
cues: Monday: the new server racks / due to arrive
Tuesday: the electrician / install extra power sockets (arranged)
Wednesday night: the team / scheduled to move the servers
Thursday: you / plan to test the network and all the services
Friday: staff / return to normal work
requiredGrammar: be due to + infinitive: The racks are due to arrive on Monday.
be scheduled to + infinitive: We're scheduled to move the servers on Wednesday night.
plan to + infinitive: I plan to test the network on Thursday.
Present continuous for future arrangements: The electrician is coming on Tuesday.
parts.sampleAnswer: Here's the plan for next week. On Monday, the new server racks are due to arrive in the morning, and we'll put them in the new room straight away. On Tuesday, the electrician is coming to install some extra power sockets, because the new room doesn't have enough. The most important day is Wednesday. The team is scheduled to move the servers on Wednesday night, after everyone has gone home, so that nobody loses any work. On Thursday, I plan to test the network and all our services, for example email and the file server. If everything works, staff are returning to normal work on Friday. I'm sending you a full timetable this afternoon.
